verdict.summary: OpenWeatherMap has no OAuth, so there is no OAuth app to register and nothing for anyone to review. You sign up, verify your email and use an API key (appid), which turns on automatically within about 2 hours. Usage limits are counted for your whole account, so every user of your agent shares your key's quota and plan.
verdict.approval_wait: none (no review; only automatic key activation of up to 2 hours)

gates.name: API key on your own account
gates.unlocks: Your agent can call the API with your appid on every request.
limits: The key can take up to 2 hours after registration to activate
Free plan covers Current Weather, 5-day/3-hour Forecast, Air Pollution, Weather Maps and Geocoding
gates.time_to_reach: About 10 minutes of work, plus up to 2 hours for the key to activate

gates.name: No test-user mode (shared account key)
gates.unlocks: There are no test-user allowlists. Anyone your agent serves uses your account's key, so once gate 1 works, invited users work too.
limits: Call limits apply to the whole account, not to each key
Any key works with every product the account subscribes to; you can't limit a key to certain products

gates.name: Production use (no review; pick a plan for your volume)
gates.unlocks: Any number of end users, limited only by your account's plan and quota.
limits: If a free account goes over its limits, OpenWeather can suspend it; HTTP 429 means a daily or monthly limit was exceeded
One Call API is pay-per-call: 1,000 free calls/day, then 0.0015 USD per call, with a default cap of 2,000 calls/day
Paid plans: Startup 40 USD/month (600 calls/min), Developer 180 USD, Professional 470 USD, Expert 1200 USD; some APIs aren't available on lower tiers
gates.time_to_reach: Right away. Upgrading the plan or adding One Call billing is self-serve.

steps.title: Create an OpenWeather account
steps.detail: Sign up at openweathermap.org. You can't open the API keys page in the developer portal without signing in.
gotchas: There is no OAuth app registration. home.openweathermap.org/oauth/authorize returns 404, so don't look for client ID/secret or redirect URI fields.

steps.title: Verify your email address
steps.detail: Click the verification link OpenWeather emails you. Once your email is verified you get your personal API key (APPID), both in a welcome email and on the API keys page.

steps.title: Create a separate API key for your agent
steps.detail: On the API keys page, create a key named for this integration (or use the default key). You can create as many keys as you like, but the account must always keep at least one.
gotchas: Separate keys don't get separate quotas. Limits are counted for the whole account.

steps.title: Wait for the key to activate
steps.detail: OpenWeather activates new keys automatically, up to 2 hours after registration. Nobody reviews them by hand.
gotchas: Calls made before activation will fail even if the key is correct. Wait before you start debugging.

steps.title: Make a test call with the key
steps.detail: Call a free-plan endpoint, such as Current Weather on api.openweathermap.org, and add your key as the appid query parameter. Some endpoints, such as One Call 3.0, are reported to also accept the key in an X-Api-Key header.

values.label: Auth parameter
values.value: appid=<your API key> (query string, on every request)

steps.title: Store the key where your agent can read it
steps.detail: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit and no managed OAuth for it. Keep the key in your own secret store, or in a custom API-key integration if you use one. You don't need a redirect URI or callback URL.

steps.title: Subscribe to One Call API 3.0 if you need it
steps.detail: One Call isn't part of the free plan. It's a separate pay-per-call subscription that requires filling in a billing form. The first 1,000 calls a day are free, then each call costs 0.0015 USD. Change the default 2,000 calls/day cap if you need to.

steps.title: Choose a plan for your total traffic and watch for 429 errors
steps.detail: Add up the expected calls from all your users, because they all share one account quota, and compare with the free limits (60/min, 1M/month) or the paid plans. Treat HTTP 429 as a quota breach and add an alert for it, since repeated overuse on the free plan can get the account suspended.

requirements.item: OpenWeather account with a verified email
requirements.detail: You get the API key only after your email is verified.

requirements.item: Plan that matches your total call volume
requirements.detail: Limits are counted for the whole account. Free is 60/min and 1M/month; paid plans start at 40 USD/month.

requirements.item: Billing form for One Call API
requirements.detail: Needed only if you use One Call (pay-per-call after 1,000 free calls/day).

requirements.item: No privacy policy, logo, review or verification
requirements.detail: OpenWeather has no OAuth app or listing process, so none of these are required.

scopes.effect: There are no OAuth scopes. Your account's subscriptions decide what you can access, and any key on the account works with every subscribed product.

blockers.symptom: You can't find an OAuth app or client ID/secret setup, and /oauth/authorize returns 404
blockers.cause: OpenWeatherMap doesn't support OAuth or OIDC at all.
blockers.fix: Use the API key (appid) from your own account instead of an OAuth connection.

blockers.symptom: A new key gets rejected right after you sign up
blockers.cause: Keys can take up to 2 hours to activate.
blockers.fix: Wait up to 2 hours, then try again.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 errors, or a warning that the account may be suspended
blockers.cause: The account went over its daily or monthly limit. All keys on the account share one quota.
blockers.fix: Cut down your calls (for example, cache responses) or move to a paid plan.

blockers.symptom: You can't find OpenWeatherMap in Composio
blockers.cause: Composio's catalog has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit.
blockers.fix: Use a custom API-key integration, or call the API directly with appid.

composio.note: Composio has no OpenWeatherMap toolkit, and OpenWeatherMap has no OAuth, so you can't start on a managed app and there's no OAuth app to register. Get an API key (appid) from your own OpenWeather account and use it through a custom API-key integration or direct HTTP calls. All usage counts against your account's quota.
